question: When an action or a movement is to be performed, which tissue will do the final job in animals?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscular tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Muscular tissue** is responsible for producing movement in animals.
 
• This tissue contracts and relaxes to cause movement, including voluntary actions like walking and involuntary actions like the beating of the heart.
 
• There are three types of muscular tissues: skeletal, smooth, and cardiac, each with distinct roles in the body.
 
• Skeletal muscles control voluntary movements, smooth muscles control involuntary actions in organs, and cardiac muscles are responsible for heartbeats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epithelial tissue**:

 
 
• It forms the covering or lining of all internal and external body surfaces.
 
• It functions in protection, absorption, secretion, and sensation.
 
 
 
• **Meristematic tissue**:
 
 
• It is found in plants and is responsible for growth.
 
• These tissues are composed of cells that can divide and differentiate into other types of cells.
 
 
 
• **Connective tissue**:
 
 
• It supports, binds together, and protects tissues and organs of the body.
 
• Includes various types like bone, blood, adipose, and cartilage.
